See also: Mamba

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Zulu imamba.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmæmbə/, /ˈmɑm.bɑ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

mamba (plural mambas)

  1. Any of various venomous snakes of the genus Dendroaspis, native to Africa, that live in trees.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • black mamba
  • green mamba

Translations

[edit]
venomous snake
  • Afrikaans: mamba, makoppa
  • Basque: manba
  • Catalan: mamba f
  • Chichewa: nsongo
  • Czech: mamba (cs) f
  • Dutch: mamba (nl) m
  • Finnish: mamba (fi)
  • French: mamba (fr) m
  • German: Mamba f
  • Italian: mamba m
  • Japanese: please add this translation if you can
  • Polish: mamba (pl) f
  • Portuguese: mamba (pt) f
  • Russian: ма́мба (ru) f (mámba)
  • Spanish: mamba (es) f
  • Swahili: please add this translation if you can
  • Zulu: imamba (zu) class 9/10

[edit]
  • mamba on Wikipedia.Wikipedia
  • Dendroaspis on Wikispecies.Wikispecies

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Probably borrowed from English mamba or Afrikaans mamba, from Zulu imamba or Swazi mamba.

Pronunciation

[edit]

  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: mam‧ba
  • Rhymes: -ɑmbaː

Noun

[edit]

mamba m (plural mamba's, no diminutive)

  1. a mamba, venomous snake of the genus Dendroaspis

Derived terms

[edit]
  • groene mamba
  • zwarte mamba
